study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Zhang et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2023
study_identification_part.si4_title: Parsing the heterogeneity of brain-symptom associations in autism spectrum disorder via random forest with homogeneous canonical correlation

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its objective to identify ASD subtypes with distinct brain–symptom association patterns using a normative model of GMV and an RFHCC algorithm. It also explains the purpose of applying normative modeling (to map individual deviations and examine heterogeneity), satisfying both criteria.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "The main aim of the current study was to test the hypothesis that there are ASD subtypes with distinct patterns of brain-symptom associations. First, we built a normative model of gray matter volume... then ... identify the ASD subtypes..."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: They built a new normative model using ABIDE controls. Eligibility and completeness are described: T1 images required; cases needed ADOS subscale scores; segmentation failures were excluded; TIV outliers were removed; final sample sizes and exclusion reasons are reported.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The study analyzed both structural neuroimaging data and phenotypic data provided by the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE)... includes the data of 571 cases ... and 1146 controls..."; "...18 participants in ABIDE I and 14 participants in ABIDE II failed to complete the segmentation... 31 samples with abnormal TIV as outliers ... were removed... requirement for ADOS subscale scores for the cases left 1146 controls and 573 cases... another 2 cases were excluded ... Finally, ... 1146 controls and 571 cases entered the following analyses."
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.location: Zhang2023.pdf.md, 2.1 Participants (line ~85); 2.2 Neuroimaging preprocessing and exclusions (around lines 119–123)

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The normative model regressed GMV on age (with polynomial up to quadratic), gender, and TIV. Multi-site effects were checked and reported to be non-significant in residuals (site assessed in eMethods 1).
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "To account for the typical development of gray matter volume (GMV), we fitted a multivariate linear regression model ... by age, gender and TIV ... model was best when the highest order of age was 2 ... the residual data did not have any significant site effect (eMethods 1)."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The neuroimaging data source for the reference cohort is explicitly stated as ABIDE (ABIDE I and II), with citations to the original publications.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The study analyzed both structural neuroimaging data and phenotypic data provided by the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) (Di Martino et al., 2017; Di Martino et al., 2014)."; "We had 1094 participants in ABIDE I and 1100 participants in ABIDE II who passed the preprocessing..."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Secondary data from ABIDE were used; no primary image acquisition was performed in this study (per guide: for SECONDARY data, answer NA).

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is described using CAT12 with specific steps (denoising, bias-correction, segmentation, normalization) and smoothing kernel; QC steps include segmentation failures and removal of TIV outliers.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "Structural neuroimaging data ... were preprocessed by using the computational anatomy toolbox 12 (CAT12)... denoising, resampling, bias-correction, affine-registration, ... unified segmentation ... partial volume estimation ... normalization by Geodesic Shooting ... smoothed with an 8-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel."; "...failed to complete the segmentation... 31 samples with abnormal TIV as outliers ... were removed."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: Although they built a new normative model, there is no description of a data partitioning strategy (e.g., held-out test set or cross-validation) specifically to evaluate normative model performance on unseen control data; the model was fit on controls and residuals applied to cases.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "To account for the typical development of GMV, we fitted a multivariate linear regression model ... using the controls ... The model was then applied to the corresponding brain regions of the cases, and the model residuals were used..."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No independent external healthy dataset was used to validate the normative model; all data were from ABIDE.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "The study analyzed ... data provided by ABIDE ... includes ... 1146 controls ..." (no mention of an external healthy validation dataset).

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: They specify the statistical model (multiple linear regression of GMV on age, gender, TIV with age up to quadratic, chosen via BIC) and key settings. However, software/libraries used to implement the normative model are not specified (only CAT12 is named for preprocessing).
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "We fitted a multivariate linear regression model ... four options for the highest order of age ... the model was the best when the highest order of age was 2 (BIC)."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: No quantitative metrics (e.g., R², prediction error, coverage) are reported for the normative model fit on the reference cohort. Site effect in residuals is discussed, but no explicit model performance metric is provided.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "... the residual data did not have any significant site effect (eMethods 1)." (no reported R²/MAE/coverage for the normative model).

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No data partitioning of the reference cohort for model development/validation is described; per guide, if no partitioning is performed, answer NA.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: They state code availability (GitHub) and data availability (ABIDE). Software version details for the normative model are not specified; preprocessing software is named (CAT12) without explicit version.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "The python code of this study is available at https://github.com/xdrzjj/ABIDE."; "The data used in this study are openly accessible through the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange..."

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Clinical cohort (ASD) is secondary data from ABIDE. Diagnostic criteria (DSM-IV-TR) are stated; data completeness and QC are described (segmentation failures, TIV outliers); and final sample sizes and exclusion reasons are reported.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "The cases were diagnosed according to DSM-IV-TR at each contributing site."; "...failed to complete the segmentation... 31 samples with abnormal TIV ... were removed ... requirement for ADOS subscale scores ... another 2 cases were excluded ... Finally ... 571 cases entered the following analyses."

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses account for demographics (age, gender, TIV), but there is no indication that clinical covariates beyond demographics (e.g., medication status, illness duration, comorbidities) were included in deviation-score analyses.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: "...we regressed out these covariates from the CC-volume and the CC-symptom scores." (covariates here are age, gender, TIV).

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: Clinical data source is specified as ABIDE with references to original publications.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "... data provided by the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) (Di Martino et al., 2017; Di Martino et al., 2014)."

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample sizes, demographics (age, sex, TIV), and clinical characteristics (ADOS, SRS, Vineland; IQ subscales) for ASD are reported.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: "Table 1. Demographic and clinical information for the subjects." (includes ASD counts, age, sex; ADOS, SRS, Vineland entries for ASD).

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Clinical measures are specified (ADOS with 3 subscales; SRS; Vineland). However, detailed assessment procedures (e.g., structured interview vs. self/clinician rating) are not described within the paper text.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: "The symptom severity was assessed by the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS), consisting of 3 subscales..."; SRS and Vineland measures listed in Table 1.

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: They explain the meaning/direction of deviation scores via associations (e.g., positive residuals indicating overgrowth linked to higher ADOS-social; negative associations and possible compensation). Quantitative thresholds to define categories are not reported.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "...33 regions had positive residuals in all ASD cases, indicating that the overgrowth of these brain regions as assessed by the normative model were associated with more severe ADOS-social scores."; "...regional volumetric deviations showed negative correlations... indicating that the overgrowth ... might be a compensation for reducing the ADOS-social symptom."
